# Support and qualification matrix

*Generated by `scripts/support-matrix.py` from [support-matrix.yaml](support-matrix.yaml). Do not edit by hand; edit the YAML and run `mise run support-matrix`. `mise run docs-check` fails when this page drifts from the YAML, or when a cell claims more than its evidence shows.*

Which versions, runtimes, harnesses, forges, trackers and gateways each Ploeg release line supports, which of them a CI job exercises, and which a dated record shows working on a live deployment. The supported deployment is profile P1 of the [threat model](../security/threat-model.md#the-supported-deployment-profile); a row outside it is unsupported even when the source implements it. "Implemented" and "qualified" are different claims: the README lists what the source contains, this page lists what is supported and what evidence stands behind it. Each cell links to its evidence, and each limit says what the evidence does not cover. Every live record comes from one environment, the maintainer's own cluster, and holds only there.

## What a cell means

| Status | Meaning | The check requires |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qualified-live` | A dated research record shows it working against a live deployment or service, at the named release or commit. | a research record under `docs/research/` that names the release or commit (`at`) and contains the quoted result |
| `tested-in-ci` | A CI job that runs on every change or on a schedule exercises it. | a job that exists in a workflow triggered by push, pull request or schedule, whose text contains the quoted versions; a named Go test must exist and, if it skips by default, the job must contain what enables it |
| `supported` | Inside the supported profile and documented, but no CI job or live record exercises it. | a page that states the requirement, containing the quoted text |
| `experimental` | Implemented or plausible, outside what anything tests. It may work; nothing here says it does. | a limits note saying what is untested |
| `unsupported` | Outside the supported profile. The chart refuses it under `supportProfile: P1` where it can see it. | a page that states the exclusion, containing the quoted text |

| 0.2.0-rc.N | current | The 0.2.0 candidates cut from `development` on every releasable merge (ADR 0116). A qualified-live cell names the candidate it was qualified at; later candidates inherit it only through the CI rows that run on every change. |
| v0.2.0 | planned | The first 0.2 stable, a soaked candidate promoted by fast-forwarding `main` (ADR 0158). Not released. It runs the candidate's digests, so it carries the candidate's cells. It is also gated by G1 to G7 of the stable channel plan, including an outsider completing the quickstart (#12). Going from 0.1 to 0.2 is a reinstall. |

## Kubernetes

The `worker-admission` job starts kind at the oldest and newest Kubernetes the worker admission policy supports, and the quickstart runs a full install and one Run on kind 0.33.0's default node, `kindest/node:v1.37.0`. No live record names the Kubernetes version of the cluster it ran on.

No job or record runs 1.29. |
| 1.30 | tested-in-ci | tested-in-ci | [CI `ci` / `worker-admission`](../../.github/workflows/ci.yml)<br>[self-hosting security](../ops/self-hosting-security.md) | The API server admits every rendered worker pod and refuses each hostile variant. No Run executes on 1.30. |
| 1.31 to 1.36 | supported | supported | [ci.yml worker-admission step](../../.github/workflows/ci.yml)<br>[toolchains](../how-to/give-runs-a-toolchain-and-checks.md) | Between the two versions CI tests; none of them is run. Toolchain image volumes need 1.35. |
| 1.37 | tested-in-ci | tested-in-ci | [CI `ci` / `worker-admission`](../../.github/workflows/ci.yml)<br>[CI `quickstart` / `run`](../../.github/workflows/quickstart.yml)<br>[mise.toml](../../mise.toml) | The quickstart creates its cluster without `--image`, so it runs kind 0.33.0's default node, the same `kindest/node:v1.37.0` digest `worker-admission` pins. The egress probe ran under runc; under Kata only the public forge address was seen refused. The allowlist is per namespace and port, not per pod. |

## In release notes

A stable release's notes carry a Qualification section ([stable channel plan](../ops/stable-channel-plan.md#changelog-upgrade-notes-and-deprecations)). Generate it from this matrix with `mise run support-matrix -- --notes 0.2.0 --commit <promoted commit>` and paste it into the release's notes. Every release's generated notes name this page at the release's own commit, so the matrix a release points to is the one that was true when it was cut.
